archetype: Mardu Vampire go-wide linear aggro that kills by trigger rather than by combat — eminence mints a body per Vampire spell, three replacement-effect doublers multiply it, and four each-opponent payoffs convert creature entries into damage at all three seats at once. strategic_frame.json says exactly this and the measurements agree: 30 creatures, 11 threats, and the two best-assembling components in the deck are the lords (83.2%) and the token multipliers (78.2%).
verdict: This deck functions and converts. Land drops hit 92.5% by turn three, the lords assemble in 83.2% of games and the token multipliers in 78.2%, and stack 009 verifies three converters composing on one two-mana Vampire for exactly 12 damage per opponent. What limits it is the answer suite, and the audit's headline hides it: interaction reads OVER at 12 and protection OVER at 9, but four of the twelve remove no permanent at all, and three of the nine — Mondrak, Purphoros and Strefan — reach only one creature each: Mondrak and Purphoros keep themselves indestructible and nobody else, and Strefan's grant rides on a Vampire arriving from hand tapped and attacking. Reading the oracle text of all 97 maindeck cards, exactly one — Anguished Unmaking — can remove an opposing ARTIFACT OR ENCHANTMENT of mana value 3 or less, and that is the class both of this deck's kill routes are shut off from: Torpor Orb at mana value 2 blanks the whole four-card converter component, and Ghostly Prison, Propaganda and Ensnaring Bridge at 3 blank the combat kill. Two white catch-alls close both halves, and the second is funded by the one painful cut.

single_points_of_failure.component: An answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment (Despark, Anguished Unmaking)
single_points_of_failure.why: This deck has two kill routes and they are blanked by different permanents, so the answer has to cover both halves. Route one is the four-card converter component — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight — which pays on a creature entering and needs no combat step at all; Torpor Orb ('Creatures entering don't cause abilities to trigger', artifact, mana value 2) blanks all four at once, and that is the route stack 009 verifies. Route two is combat — the nine lords and anthems, Sanctum Seeker's attack trigger, Edgar's own — and Ghostly Prison and Propaganda (enchantments, mana value 3) and Ensnaring Bridge (artifact, mana value 3) blank that one, taking Throne of the God-Pharaoh most of the way with them, because a creature that cannot attack does not tap. Two of the four blanks are artifacts and two are enchantments. Two permanents usually named alongside them are not blanks and I am dropping them from the set: Cursed Totem stops only activated abilities of creatures and reaches NONE of these routes (it taxes Bloodline Keeper, Captivating Vampire and Mondrak instead), and Authority of the Consuls makes your creatures enter tapped, which FEEDS Throne of the God-Pharaoh — its real cost is the 1 life it hands an opponent per creature. Against all four, reading all 97 maindeck cards, exactly one — Anguished Unmaking — answers an opposing artifact or enchantment of mana value 3 or less; Despark is gated to mana value 4 or greater; and nothing in the 97 removes an opposing land. deck-audit also names Feed the Swarm and Vandalblast as closers, and each covers exactly one half of the corrected set — Feed the Swarm the two enchantments, Vandalblast the two artifacts — with Vandalblast's {R} at mana value 1 asking 23 red sources against 17, the deepest single-pip shortfall in the deck. Generous Gift and Stroke of Midnight cover both halves at {2}{W}, where 21 white sources clear the 19 that row asks. Measured 30.8% drawn, 23.8% by turn six; 60.4% and 49.0% if a tutor is spent on it.

cut_candidates.why: A three-mana Human Soldier in a Vampire deck, and the type line costs it three things: no eminence token when cast, no bonus from the five Vampire-gated pumps among the nine-card lord component (Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain, Captivating Vampire, Vampire Socialite, Cordial Vampire), and no discount from Herald's Horn (Vampire-named) or Bontu's Monument (black creature spells only). Outlast at {W} is unusable at this speed. What it does contribute — a static flying grant off the deck's ten buff:counters cards — is real, which is why this is contested and not easy.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: The board's only STATIC flying grant, and one genuine pair inside the lord component: Drana, Liberator of Malakir puts a +1/+1 counter on EACH attacking creature you control with no type restriction, so she both pumps the Falconer and switches his own grant on for the whole team. Elspeth, Storm Slayer's 0 grants flying until your next turn and is repeatable, and Akroma's Will grants it for a turn, so the effect does not disappear — it becomes conditional on Elspeth surviving or on holding four mana. Against a pod with ground blockers that is a real loss of reach.

gaps: interaction-breadth reports 5 classes with none uncovered and credits 2 cards to the LAND class, and the mechanism is now known. deck_audit.py:119 matches land removal with `(destroy|exile)[^.]{0,90}\bland`, which fires on Winds of Abandon's clause 'For each creature exiled this way, its controller searches their library for a basic LAND card' — a card that RAMPS the opponent, scored as answering lands. Despark reaches the class through the any-permanent catch-all at deck_audit.py:258, whose `(destroy|exile|return|puts?|gain control of)[^.]{0,70}(target|each|all|any|another) permanent` fires on 'Exile target permanent' and then does `hits.add("land")` outright; but a land has mana value 0 and Despark needs 4 or greater. Reading all 97 I find no card that destroys, exiles or bounces an opposing land. I carry the audit's 5 unchanged and flag the disagreement; the true breadth is 4 of 5.

Cast rates are not measured anywhere. goldfish reports what is DRAWN; the colour-sources reading above is a hypergeometric yardstick from mana_analysis, not an observed failure rate. 'How often is a {1}{B}{B}{B} card stuck in hand' has no artifact.

deck_recon.json is dated 2026-08-03 and several of its findings are stale against the current decklist: it names Anguished Unmaking, Warleader's Call, Impact Tremors, Charismatic Conqueror, Command Tower, Cavern of Souls, Caretaker's Talent and Elspeth, Storm Slayer as cards the deck does not run, and the current 99 runs every one. Only the typal-mana finding and the removal-breadth reasoning are used above, and both are attributed as evidence rather than authority.

No candidate_pool.json exists for this deck, so the add candidates are drawn from deck-audit's own named closers and from recon, not from a scored pool. upgrade-facts' 25 synergy candidates are Voltron auras (All That Glitters, Ethereal Armor, Hyena Umbra) and are a format-wide top-10 artifact rather than a fit signal — none is proposed.
The deck's two contained combo lines are recorded as bracket 3 by combo_details while bracket-check forces floor 4 on the same lines. The tag is format-agnostic and is not used above; the floor is.

The colour-sources weakness gets no add and I withdraw the one I had proposed. Path of Ancestry adds one unrestricted source of each colour but enters tapped unconditionally, which contradicts lean_into[1]; and its natural cut, Spectator Seating, enters tapped only 'unless you have two or more opponents', so deck-audit files it under conditional_cards rather than taplands and the swap would have been −1 untapped source for +1 unconditional tapland. What the corrected enumeration shows instead is that eight of the nineteen under-line cards are red, and no artifact here measures whether that costs casts.

The bench cannot close the gap. I read all 29 analysable sideboard cards and not one removes an opposing permanent; the closest is Callous Bloodmage, whose third mode exiles a graveyard. One card (Runo Stromkirk // Krothuss) is outside the colour identity. Both adds above therefore have to come from the pool rather than from cards the pilot is already known to own.

findings.note: FIX 1 VERIFIED, and it is now the same claim as axes[8] rather than a compatible one. deck-audit's protection axis measures 9 copies and its measured.cards list contains all three named cards (Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Deflecting Swat, Flawless Maneuver, Mondrak, Purphoros, Strefan, Swiftfoot Boots, Teferi's Protection), so 'three of the nine' is drawn from the audit's own membership. I read all three oracle texts out of cards.json: Mondrak is '{1}{W/P}{W/P}, Sacrifice two other artifacts and/or creatures: Put an indestructible counter on Mondrak' (itself and nobody else); Purphoros carries the bare keyword 'Indestructible' (itself and nobody else); Strefan reads 'Whenever Strefan attacks, you may sacrifice two Blood tokens. If you do, you may put a Vampire card from your hand onto the battlefield tapped and attacking. It gains indestructible until end of turn' — one creature, arriving from hand, exactly as written. 'Reach only one creature each' is true of all three and the false pass-2 premise ('protect no creature that is already on the board') is gone rather than annotated. axes[8] says Mondrak and Purphoros carry indestructibility 'for themselves alone' and Strefan 'protects nothing that is already on the board'; the verdict's two sub-clauses are the same two facts, compressed.
